svg.title: A plan is classified high or low risk first; low-risk plans trade design review for red tests
svg.desc: A plan is first classified by a mechanical gate. High-risk plans (money, outbound messages, irreversible data, guard code) go through the design review loop. Low-risk plans skip design review: each acceptance clause binds a test that must be red now; at push time the gate re-classifies, re-runs those tests, and small manual-only changes pass a diffusion/size/history/purpose check. Code review by diff risk still applies to both.
svg.text: Once a plan is written, classify it first: high risk / low risk
The test: after reverting the commit, is there anything outside the repo left to clean up by hand?
Plan note
acceptance clauses [S1]… each bound to a test
Spec gate: lumos spec-gate (mechanical, defaults to high risk)
Keywords for money / outbound sends / irreversible data / guard code,
links to risk-tagged notes, or the author's own flag → high risk
High risk: design review as usual
• Multi-seat review loop; disposal gate must pass first
• Clauses may be manual; a rollback section is required
• Bound tests run once; red/green printed, not blocking
• Linked notes' contract tests join acceptance; red blocks
Low risk: red tests replace design review
• Hazards section rules out all four classes, one line each
• New clauses must be red now; [keeps] ones green
• Pass → implement directly; record door, tests, fingerprint
• Small changes may be manual-only; push runs a size gate
Implement
Push gate (pre-push)
Low-risk plans: re-classify, compare the clause fingerprint, run every recorded test; manual-only: diffusion / size / history / purpose
Both kinds still get code review by diff risk (architecture seat at every tier); escapes are logged and fed back
Red at the spec gate, green at the push gate: "said it's done" and "actually done" pinned from both ends
